newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 28.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 28.

text.p: News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends

BERLIN - Private television station Sat1 says it has signed up licensing agennecy BMC of Munich to market its booming merchandise sales. BMC will take on marketing activities for Sat1 licensed products which are not advertised on-air, effective June 1, the station says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Germans are drinking less milk, but are eating more yoghurt and cheese. Average individual milk consumption dropped by 1.76 kilograms in 1996 to 63.1 litres. Dairy production however increased last year to 27.2 million tonnes from 26.8 million in 1995. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
BONN - Federal post minister Wolfgang Boetsch will decide on a policy on digital technology in the television arena in the coming weeks, all-news network n-tv says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Analysts from the BHF Bank say they estimate the fair value of Pro Sieben AG shares between 70 and 80 marks ($41 and $47), but say it is probable the price will drop after its debut. They call the German television market is more intensely competitive than the international TV market. Pro Sieben plans to list its shares on German stock exchanges and in a private placement in New York in mid-summer. (Reuter)

NUREMBERG - Media market research company GfK says it is considering a public share listing in 1999. The company plans to evaulate the general stock market situation, its own development and the market before taking a decision. It says it plans to expand consolidated group turnover to over 650 million marks before 2000. (Reuter)

STUTTGART - Daimler-Benz AG Chairman Juergen Schrempp says he expects 1997 car sales to climb to over 700,000 from 645,000 in 1996. He also says European truck orders were up 45 percent in the first four months of 1997. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Auto parts group Ymos AG says net profits dipped 13 percent last year, but the results were heavily affected by extraordinary income and costs, and profits were expected to improve. Group net profit last year fell 2.4 billion marks to 16.4 billion marks as sales rose seven billion marks to 957 billion marks. (Reuter)

BONN - Retail giant Metro AG, born of a merger with three store chains last year, impresses investors by hitting 1996 profit targets and says it will seek to expand its business internationally. Metro says it made 1.062 billion marks in group income on ordinary activities and 717 million marks in net profits. (Reuter)
MANNHEIM - Building group Bilfinger + Berger Bau AG says it is looking abroad to boost earnings in 1997 as a crisis in Germany's construction sector hits domestic output. (Reuter)
